EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  
────────────────────────────────────────

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  
Strategy:  Within-family (sibling) fixed-effects estimation, complemented by an event-study on repeated test scores.  

Why appropriate:  
•  55 % of the CNLSY mothers have both a Head-Start child and a non-Head-Start sibling, giving naturally matched “treatment–control” pairs.  
•  Mother fixed effects purge all time-invariant family and maternal attributes (genetics, parenting style, race, permanent income, neighbourhood selection, etc.).  
•  Remaining variation in treatment is driven largely by (i) program slot expansions during the mid-1980s, (ii) child birth-cohort differences within the same family, and (iii) the two-year cap on participation.  
•  Repeated PPVT/PIAT tests allow an event-study specification to trace fade-out/ re-emergence patterns.  

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  
Treatment variable  
HS_i  = 1 if child i ever attended Head Start at ages 3–4 (modal enrolment year); 0 otherwise.

Control groups  
Primary: own siblings who attended no pre-school (counterfactual = home care).  
Secondary: siblings who attended non-Head-Start preschool (to isolate the incremental effect relative to alternative centre-based care).

Timing / Event date  
For cognitive outcomes we index time by “years since the Fall immediately preceding kindergarten start” (t = –1 pre-test, t = 0 kindergarten year, t = 1,2… through age 14).  
For young-adult outcomes we measure at first interview age ≥19.

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  
A1. Family invariance: All unobserved determinants that are constant within a mother do not interact with treatment (guaranteed by mother FE).  
A2. No systematic family-level trend aligned with treatment: Any time-varying family shocks (e.g., income growth, union formation, moves) are either uncorrelated with which sibling receives Head Start or can be controlled by rich child-specific covariates and birth-order/year-of-birth dummies.  
A3. No cross-sibling spillovers (SUTVA): One child’s participation does not directly change a sibling’s outcome except through resource re-allocation that is uncorrelated with treatment.  
A4. Correct reporting: Mis-classification of Head Start attendance is non-differential with respect to outcomes.  
Plausibility: A1 guaranteed; A2 plausible because program slot expansions were exogenous to the family, yet we will test. A3 may be violated (see threats). A4 plausible—survey questions name “Head Start” explicitly, but we will test with program availability instruments.

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION  

Threat 1: Birth-order / cohort bias  
Head Start slots expanded over time; later-born siblings are more likely treated and may differ systematically.  
•  Include birth-order and birth-year dummies interacted with mother FE.  
•  Restrict to siblings ≤4 years apart as robustness.  
•  Event-study pre-treatment trend test on PPVT/PIAT at age 3 (before enrolment).

Threat 2: Sibling spillovers (under-identification of total family effect)  
•  Show that siblings’ outcomes are unrelated to a sibling’s treatment when the sibling herself is too old to have been eligible (placebo test).  
•  Estimate lower-bound (within-family) and upper-bound (between-family) effects to bracket true impact.

Threat 3: Selection into “other preschools”  
If the no-preschool sibling is not the true counterfactual because parents would have bought alternate care absent Head Start.  
•  Estimate triple-difference: (HS – NoPS) – (OtherPS – NoPS) within mother to net out generic preschool effects.  
•  Control for county×year private preschool supply measures.

5. R CODE OUTLINE  

```r
# Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# 1. Load data -----------------------------------------------------------------
cnlsy <- fread("cnlsy_child_level.csv")          # one row per child

# 2. Variable construction -----------------------------------------------------
cnlsy[ , HS := (preschool_type == "HeadStart")]
cnlsy[ , OtherPS := (preschool_type == "OtherPreschool")]
cnlsy[ , NoPS := (preschool_type == "None")]

# Long-form repeated test scores (assumed already stacked)
# Event time relative to kindergarten entry
cnlsy[ , ev_time := test_year - (birth_year + 5)]  # kindergarten at 5

# Outcome examples
cnlsy[ , gradHS := (educ_attain >= 12)]
cnlsy[ , idle   := (hours_work==0 & school_enroll==0)]

# 3. Main specification --------------------------------------------------------
# (a) Long-run outcomes – sibling fixed effects
spec_long <- feols(gradHS ~ HS + OtherPS + birth_order + birth_year |
                   mother_id, data = cnlsy, cluster = "mother_id")
summary(spec_long)

# (b) Event-study for test scores
est_event <- feols(PPVT_score ~ i(ev_time, HS, ref = -1) + birth_order |
                   mother_id + child_id,  # child FE absorbs level
                   data = cnlsy[abs(ev_time)<=6], cluster="mother_id")
iplot(est_event, ci=TRUE, ref.line = 0)

# 4. Robustness check: restrict to sibs ≤4 years apart
close_sib <- cnlsy[ , .SD[ max(birth_year) - min(birth_year) <=4 ], by = mother_id]
spec_rb <- feols(gradHS ~ HS + OtherPS + birth_order + birth_year |
                 mother_id, data = close_sib, cluster="mother_id")
coeftest(spec_rb, vcov. = vcovCL, cluster = ~mother_id)
```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS  
Theory and existing small-scale experiments suggest a 0.10–0.20 σ gain in early test scores that fades to ~0 by age ten but re-emerges in human-capital outcomes.  Anticipated magnitudes (treated vs. own sibling control):  
•  High-school graduation ↑ 4–6 pp (baseline 78 %).  
•  Grade retention ↓ 3 pp.  
•  College attendance ↑ 2 pp.  
•  Idleness ↓ 4 pp; Crime ↓ 2 pp.  
•  Larger gains for Black children and for children of low-AFQT mothers.

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (Sibling FE design)  
C1: Families have both treated & control child (common-support) …………………… 1  
C2: No differential pre-treatment trends within family …………………………………… 1  
C3: No time-varying family shocks correlated with treatment ………………………… 0  
C4: No spillovers across siblings (SUTVA) …………………………………………………… 0  
C5: Accurate measurement of treatment & outcomes …………………………………… 1  
Total = 3 / 5  → Evidence is promising but not bullet-proof; robustness tests above directly target C3-C4.
